ip_top_stories.title: Publishers, bestselling author sue Google over Gemini AI book training in New York court
ip_top_stories.summary: A group of publishers and a bestselling author have filed suit against Google in New York, alleging the company used copyrighted books to train its Gemini AI models without authorisation. The case adds to a growing body of litigation targeting major AI developers over training data practices. No licensing agreement or fair use defence has been publicly disclosed by Google at this stage.

ip_top_stories.title: How Anthropic ended up paying $1.5bn for training Claude on pirated books
ip_top_stories.summary: A detailed account of Anthropic's $1.5 billion settlement arising from its use of pirated books to train the Claude AI model. The piece examines how the company sourced training data and the legal consequences that followed. It represents one of the largest financial outcomes yet in AI copyright litigation.

ip_top_stories.title: AI labs buy up, rip pages from books to train models
ip_top_stories.summary: Reporting reveals that AI laboratories have been purchasing physical books and digitising their contents — including by removing pages — to build training datasets for large language models. The practice raises fresh copyright questions about the extent to which AI developers are circumventing existing digital licensing arrangements. The story has been covered by multiple outlets, with the primary source selected here.

ip_top_stories.title: US musicians' union files amended lawsuit against Universal and Warner over Suno and Udio AI deals
ip_top_stories.summary: The American Federation of Musicians has filed an amended lawsuit against Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group, alleging the labels struck deals with AI music generators Suno and Udio that harm musicians' rights. The complaint targets licensing arrangements the union argues were made without adequate regard for performers' copyright interests. The case marks a significant escalation in labour and copyright disputes over AI-generated music.

ip_top_stories.title: Bipartisan bill would address AI, copyright concerns in creative industries
ip_top_stories.summary: A bipartisan legislative proposal has been introduced in the US Congress aimed at addressing copyright protections for creators in the context of AI training and output. The bill reflects growing political pressure to establish clearer rules around AI use of copyrighted material in the creative sector. Specific provisions have not yet been fully detailed in public reporting.

ip_further_links.title: Is training an AI model 'public interest'? Delhi HC verdict goes to heart of copyright debate
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of a Delhi High Court ruling that examines whether AI model training can be justified as a public interest activity under copyright law, a question with wide implications for how fair use and similar doctrines apply to AI developers globally.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI secures first win in India copyright row against ANI
ip_further_links.summary: OpenAI has secured an initial legal victory in India in its copyright dispute with news agency ANI, marking the first such court outcome for the company in the country.

ip_further_links.title: Canadian music publishers argue only humans should qualify as copyright authors in AI case
ip_further_links.summary: Canadian music publishers have made submissions in an AI copyright case asserting that authorship under copyright law should be restricted to human creators, a position that could have significant implications for AI-generated works.

ip_further_links.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX AI won't destroy rare books for AI training as Anthropic's scanning practices face scrutiny
ip_further_links.summary: Elon Musk publicly stated that SpaceX's AI operations will not destroy rare books for training purposes, as Anthropic faces increased scrutiny over its physical book scanning practices.

ip_further_links.title: Artists are lawyering up against AI slop, and some are even winning
ip_further_links.summary: A report on visual artists pursuing copyright claims against AI companies for unauthorised use of their work in training data, with some artists beginning to achieve favourable legal outcomes.

ip_further_links.title: ASCAP CEO Elizabeth Matthews on embracing AI opportunities while protecting songwriters from 'theft'
ip_further_links.summary: ASCAP's CEO outlines the organisation's position on AI and music copyright, advocating for licensing frameworks that compensate songwriters while engaging constructively with AI opportunities.

ip_further_links.title: An artist is suing an AI meme generator for selling his viral comic as ad templates
ip_further_links.summary: Artist Elmer Saflor has filed a copyright infringement suit against an AI-powered memes generator that allegedly sold his viral comic as commercial advertising templates without permission.

ip_further_links.title: CopySight Raises $3 Million Seed Round to Expand AI Copyright Risk Platform
ip_further_links.summary: CopySight has raised $3 million in seed funding to develop a platform designed to help businesses identify and manage copyright risk arising from generative AI use.

ip_further_links.title: The Hidden Cost of Trust
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines the risks academic publishers face when extending trust to AI-related partnerships and data-sharing arrangements, with implications for intellectual property and institutional credibility.

ip_further_links.title: Indonesia consults digital platforms, media on AI copyright framework
ip_further_links.summary: Indonesia's government is consulting with digital platforms and media organisations as it develops a national framework to address copyright issues arising from AI, reflecting growing regulatory activity in Southeast Asia.
